content:
incident-bot: PAGING — elevated 5xx and timeouts observed in eu-central-1 edge proxy pool. alert level: P2. affected route: /v1/generate -> model-gateway eu-c-gw-1. auto-steer kicked in.

alice: I'm on it. pulling proxy + gateway metrics now. any recent proxy config changes?

samir: seeing a sharp backend latency jump starting ~07:12 UTC. spikes align with model-gateway 502s. grafana: https://grafana.company/graph?panelId=502-euc 

priya: there was a timeout tuning patch deployed at 06:50 UTC to lower backend timeout to 2s. i'm going to revert that patch now.

devops-bot: Revert job queued by priya. Job ID: revert-20260315-671.

alice: temporarily steering 10% of eu-central-1 traffic -> eu-west-1 to blunt customer impact (policy: soft-steer). will monitor.

laura-support: CS: two customers reported bulk 502s and timeouts, opened incidents INC-9981 and INC-9982. pinged enterprise success, drafting status note.

samir: logs show repeated upstream ECONNRESET and 502s from gw instances:
```
[2026-03-15T07:16:23Z] gw/conn.go: read tcp 10.0.5.2:443: connection reset by peer
[proxy] route=eu-c-gw-1 req_id=7a2b... status=502 latency_ms=2123
```

miguel: redis latency looks normal. I do see memory pressure on a subset of model workers in eu-c-region; swap activity spike around 07:10. Could be worker OOMs causing resets.

priya: rollback complete at 07:22 UTC (revert-20260315-671). observing partial improvement but errors still above baseline.

alice: starting targeted drain of edgepool eu-c-edge-2 and shifting traffic to eu-c-edge-3; ETA ~2m. will preserve warm KV caches where possible.

oncall-next: taking over from alice for the monitoring window. I'll hold page and keep an eye on the steering. prepping handoff notes.

samir: increasing fallback steering to eu-west-1 -> 35% to reduce pressure while we stabilize underlying workers.

laura-support: posted customer-facing note: "We're aware of intermittent 5xx errors in EU-Central and have applied mitigations; some requests may still experience errors while we finish stabilization." shared link to status page. :white_check_mark:

devops-bot: Deploy bot detected a canary deploy at 07:24 UTC and has automatically paused it due to elevated error rate. Canary ID: canary-3421.

samir: current error rate ~0.6% (peak ~2.1%). baseline is ~0.02%. trending down after revert + steering.

alice: creating incident channel #inc-2418675309 for postmortem and follow-ups. assigning triage owners.

priya: follow-ups: 1) correlate memory/heap growth on model workers with request patterns during 07:00-07:20, 2) validate why the shorter timeout caused cascading resets, 3) review canary gating rules. assigning to samir and me.

miguel: I'll take the customer impact summary and coordinate with CS for a timeline + root cause info for impacted accounts.

oncall-next: handing back monitoring to ops rotation; I'll document what I saw and include relevant logs. keeping watch for one hour.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied (rollback + edge steering + pool drain). observed error rate reduced; severity downgraded to P3. last observed significant spike: 07:26 UTC.

alice: thanks team. immediate win: rollback + steering prevented broader outage. next steps in postmortem: heap dumps from model workers, deeper proxy connection tracing, revisit timeout tuning and canary thresholds.

laura-support: once postmortem draft is ready, I'll prepare a customer-facing summary.

samir: logging collected and snapshot saved to s3://incidents/2418675309/logs.tar.gz. will attach graphs to postmortem.

oncall-next: taking the incident forward for the next shift; leaving the channel in read-only for now. if error rate creeps up, re-page oncall.

alice: closing urgent remediation loop. thanks all — great fast triage.
